subject: left-handedness
title: What If Everyone Were Left-Handed?

scenes.text: What if everyone on Earth were left-handed? Lefties would lose their secret weapon overnight.
Today about one person in ten is left-handed, according to a study of nearly two and a half million people.
Flip that, and every right-handed pair of scissors and can opener suddenly feels backwards in nine hands out of ten.
Sport changes most. About thirty percent of top baseball pitchers are left-handed, three times their share of the population.
Among top male table tennis players, it's about a quarter. Opponents rarely face lefties, so their angles feel unfamiliar.
Make everyone left-handed, and that edge flips. The rare right-handers become the ones nobody is ready for.

description:
What if everyone were left-handed? The biggest handedness study, covering about 2.4 million people, puts left-handers at about 10.6%.
In sports with high time pressure lefties are overrepresented: about 30% of top baseball pitchers and about 26% of top male table tennis players. One explanation is surprise, because opponents rarely practise against them, and that edge only works while lefties are rare.
